---
title: "About Me"
description: "Background and CV of Giovanni Cuttica."
---

I graduated in Political Science and Governmental Studies at the University of Turin. During my Master's thesis, I developed a strong interest in policy evaluation and decided to continue my studies in this field, joining a course in Policy Analysis and Evaluation promoted by the Italian Parliament and the University of Venice.

After obtaining that degree, I started working as a junior researcher at *IRES Piemonte* (the regional research institute of Italy's Piemonte region). I worked there mainly on policy evaluation of European-funded programs (ERDF and ESF) and regional economic analysis. 

After several years focused on empirical research, I realized I wanted to pursue a PhD to deepen my knowledge and be able to answer more challenging research questions. In 2023, I enrolled in the PhD in Economics at the University of Ferrara, under the supervision of [Prof. Leonzio Rizzo](https://sites.google.com/view/leonzio-rizzo/home).

During my PhD, I had the opportunity to spend almost a year as a visiting student at Carlos III University of Madrid (Spain), where I took several courses to strengthen my econometrics knowledge and deepen my understanding of my research topics.

Right now, I am polishing my PhD dissertation, which sits at the intersection of local public finance and political economy. The first chapter studies the effects of intermunicipal cooperation on property tax collection and evasion. The second chapter examines a disaster event — the 2023 flood in Emilia-Romagna — and how local governments managed it, showing the effects of intermunicipal cooperation on disaster management. The third chapter, also set in the Italian municipal context, focuses on the Political Budget Cycle and land use.

### Not academic "me"

When I am not behind a computer running regressions, my life is mostly about spending time in nature, primarily with my wife Francesca and with our friends.

I'm totally obsessed with rock climbing. I'm a decent climber, far from the top level of amateurs, but I've been climbing for more than fifteen years and I have a lot of fun doing it. I am also a (weak) road cyclist, but I am really (really) good at pain management: I am an honored finisher of the "Maddanes" (if you know, you know), and my top *sufferfest* was the mighty Susa-Susa, a 200km ride with more than 4500m of climbing between the Italian and French Alps.

I also enjoy trying to learn new things — for example, the last rabbit hole I fell into was carving and woodworking, but, to be honest, I am far from being "ok".
